chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of his father, and a number of our companions, all from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Abu Ziyad Al-Karkhy, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was born in Kutha Ruba, and his father was from its people. The mother of Ibrahim and the mother of Lut were Sara and Warqa' (and in one copy, Ruqayya), two sisters, and they were both daughters of Lahij. And Lahij was a Prophet, a Warner, but was not a Messenger. And Ibrahim (peace be upon him) in his youth was upon the natural disposition upon which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the creation, until Allah, Blessed and High, guided him to His religion and chose him.

And indeed he married Sara, the daughter of Lahij, and she was the daughter of his maternal aunt. And Sara was the owner of much livestock, vast land, and good financial condition. And she had granted Ibrahim (peace be upon him) ownership of all that she owned, so he managed it and improved it, and the livestock and crops increased until there was no man in the land of Kutha Ruba who had a better condition than him.

And when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) broke the idols of Nimrod, Nimrod ordered that he be captured and bound. They built a platform for him, gathered firewood in it, and ignited the fire, then threw Ibrahim (peace be upon him) into the fire to burn him. Then they withdrew from it until the fire extinguished. Then they looked at the platform, and there was Ibrahim (peace be upon him) safe and sound, released from his bonds. So Nimrod was informed of his news, and he ordered them to exile Ibrahim (peace be upon him) from their land and prevent him from leaving with his livestock and wealth.

So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) disputed with them regarding that, saying: 'If you take my livestock and my wealth, then my right upon you is that you return to me what has passed of my lifetime in your land.' They argued before the judge of Nimrod, who ruled that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) should surrender to them all that he had acquired in their land, and ruled against the companions of Nimrod that they should return to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) what had passed of his lifetime in their land. When Nimrod was informed of this, he ordered them to clear his path and the path of his livestock and wealth, and to expel him, saying: 'If he remains in your land, he will corrupt your religion and harm your gods.' So they expelled Ibrahim and Lut (peace be upon them both) from their land to Syria.

So Ibrahim went out with Lut, who did not leave him, and Sara. He said to them: 'I am going to my Lord; He will guide me,' meaning Bayt Al-Maqdis. So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) took his livestock and wealth, and made a carriage (Taboot), and placed Sara in it, and locked it with locks due to his modesty for her. He proceeded until he exited the authority of Nimrod and came to the authority of a man from the Copts called Araarat.

So he passed by a tax collector of his, and the tax collector stopped him to tax what was with him. When he reached the tax collector with the carriage, the tax collector said to Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Open this carriage so we may tax what is in it.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Say whatever you like of gold or silver from it, so we may pay its tithe, but do not open it.' The tax collector refused except to open it, and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was angry at its opening.

When Sara appeared to him, and she was described with beauty and elegance, the tax collector said to him: 'What is this woman to you?' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'She is my sanctity (wife) and the daughter of my aunt.' The tax collector said to him: 'So what prompted you to hide her in this carriage?' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'Modesty for her, lest anyone see her.' The tax collector said: 'I will not let you depart until I inform the king of her condition and yours.'

So he sent a messenger to the king and informed him. The king sent a messenger from him to bring them the carriage. They came to take it, and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to them: 'I will not leave the carriage until my soul leaves my body.' They informed the king of that, so the king sent: 'Carry him and the carriage with him.'

So they carried Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and the carriage and all that was with him until he was brought to the king. The king said to him: 'Open the carriage.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'O King! In it is my sanctity and the daughter of my aunt, and I am ransoming its opening with all that is with me.'

The king got angry at its opening. When he saw Sara, his patience could not contain his foolishness, so he extended his hand to her. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) turned his face away from her and from him due to his modesty, and said: 'O Allah! Withhold his hand from my sanctity and the daughter of my aunt!' So his hand did not reach her, nor did it return to him.

The king said to him: 'Is it your God who did this to me?' He said to him: 'Yes. Indeed, my God is Modest (Ghayour), who dislikes the prohibited, and He is the One who placed a barrier between you and what you intended of the prohibited.'

The king said to him: 'So supplicate to your God that He return my hand to me. If He answers you, I will not present myself to her.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'My God! Return his hand to him so he may refrain from my sanctity.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, returned his hand to him.

The king turned his gaze toward her, then extended his hand toward her. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) turned his face away from him due to his modesty, and said: 'O Allah! Withhold his hand from her.' So his hand withered and did not reach her.

The king said to Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, your God is Modest, and indeed you are modest. So supplicate to your God that He return my hand to me, for if He does, I will not repeat.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'I will ask Him that upon the condition that if you repeat, you do not ask me to ask Him.' The king said: 'Yes.'
So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah! If he is truthful, return his hand to him.' So his hand returned to him.

When the king saw from the modesty what he saw, and saw the sign in his hand, he magnified Ibrahim (peace be upon him), feared him, honored him, and respected him. He said to him: 'You are safe from me presenting myself to her or to anything with you, so go wherever you wish, but I have a need from you.'

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'What is it?' He said to him: 'I love that you permit me to serve her with a Coptic woman who is with me, beautiful and intelligent, who will be her servant.' So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) gave him permission. He called for her and gifted her to Sara, and she is Hajar, mother of Ismail (peace be upon him).

So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) traveled with all that was with him, and the king came out with him, walking behind Ibrahim (peace be upon him) out of respect for him and awe of him. So Allah, Blessed and High, revealed to Ibrahim: 'Stop and do not walk in front of the domineering tyrant while he walks behind you, but make him in front of you and walk, and magnify him and honor him, for he is a ruler, and there must be authority in the earth, whether righteous or immoral.'

So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) stopped and said to the king: 'Proceed, for my God has revealed to me at this moment that I should magnify you and honor you, and that I should place you in front of me and walk behind you out of respect for you.'

The king said to him: 'Has this been revealed to you?' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Yes.' The king said to him: 'I testify that surely your God is Friendly, Lenient, Generous, and indeed you make me incline toward your religion.' And the king bade them farewell.

So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) traveled until he encamped at the high places of Syria, and left Lut (peace be upon him) in the low places of Syria. Then, when the child was delayed for him, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to Sara: 'If you wish, sell Hajar to me, perhaps Allah will grant us a child from her, who will be a successor for us.' So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) bought Hajar from Sara, and he went to her, and she gave birth to Ismail (peace be upon him).

key_terms.التَّابُوت: Carriage/Box, a container used to transport Sara
key_terms.اللَّاحِج: Lahij, father of Sara and mother of Lut
key_terms.كُوثَى رُبَا: Kutha Ruba, the place of Ibrahim's birth

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and the Coptic king in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Kafi, transmitted via the chain of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, elaborates on the pre-prophetic life of Ibrahim (AS), highlighting his noble lineage and the miraculous preservation of his wife Sara from the Coptic king Araarat as a sign of divine favor. It details the legalistic dispute over his wealth and the subsequent gift of Hajar, illustrating the practical wisdom and modesty (ghayrah) characteristic of the prophets in Shia tradition. The account serves to contextualize the origins of the Ishmaelite line and the interplay between divine decree and human agency in the history of monotheism.

en.hubeali: H 15007 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, together from Al-Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Ziyad Al-Karkhy who said: ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying that: ‘Ibrahimas was born at Kowsy Ruba, and hisas father was from its inhabitants, and the mother of Ibrahimas, and the mother of Lutas were Sara and Warqa’ (and in another copy ‘Ruqayya’), and were sisters, and they were both the daughters of Lahijas. And Lahijas was a Prophetas, a Warner, but was not a Messengeras. And Ibrahimas was, in hisas youth, upon the nature which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Created, to the extent that Allahazwj Blessed and High Guided himas to Hisazwj Religion, and Chose himas.

And he<sup>as</sup> married Sara, the daughter of Lahij<sup>as</sup>, the daughter of his<sup>as</sup> maternal aunt. And Sara was the owner of a lot of assets, and vast lands, and of good financial condition, and Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> was the owner of all what she had owned. So he<sup>as</sup> managed it, and corrected the affairs, and increased the assets and plantations considerably, to the extent that he<sup>as</sup> became the most affluent man in the land of Kowsy Ruba.

And when Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> broke the idols, Nimrod<sup>la</sup> ordered his<sup>as</sup> capture, and they built a platform, and gathered the firewood around it and ignited the fire, and threw Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> via a catapult to be burnt by it. Then they relaxed until the fire burnt out. Then they looked at the platform and there was Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, safe and sound, but the ropes that he<sup>as</sup> was bound by had been burnt to ashes. So they informed Nimrod<sup>la</sup> of his<sup>as</sup> news. So he<sup>la</sup> ordered them to exile Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> from his<sup>as</sup> city, and prevent him<sup>as</sup> from the taking his<sup>as</sup> assets and his<sup>as</sup> wealth with him<sup>as</sup>.

So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> disputed with them with regards to that. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘If you<sup>as</sup> are confiscating my<sup>as</sup> assets and my<sup>as</sup> wealth, therefore it is my<sup>as</sup> right against you that you should return to me<sup>as</sup> what has gone from my<sup>as</sup> lifetime in your city’, and he<sup>as</sup> argued against the judge of Nimrod<sup>la</sup>, so he judged that Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> should submit to him<sup>la</sup> all of what he<sup>as</sup> had acquired in their city, and that Nimrod<sup>la</sup> to return what had gone from his<sup>as</sup> life. The news of that reached Nimrod<sup>la</sup>, so he<sup>la</sup> ordered that they should open the way for him<sup>as</sup> and allow him<sup>as</sup> to take his<sup>as</sup> assets, and his<sup>as</sup> wealth, and throw him<sup>as</sup> out from their city to Syria.

So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> went out, and with him<sup>as</sup> was Lut<sup>as</sup> who would not separate from him<sup>as</sup>, and Sara, and said to them: ‘I<sup>as</sup> am going to my<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> to be Guided by Him<sup>azwj</sup>’ – meaning Bayt Al-Maqdis. So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> took his<sup>as</sup> assets, and his<sup>as</sup> wealth, and constructed a carriage (Taboot), and made Sara to be in it, and locked it with locks, due to his<sup>as</sup> honour from it, and went until he<sup>as</sup> exited from the authority of Nimrod<sup>la</sup> and went to the authority of a man from the Coptics called Araarat.

So they passed by a tax collector of his. The tax collector stopped him<sup>as</sup> in order to tax him<sup>as</sup> for what was with him<sup>as</sup>. So when he<sup>as</sup> ended up with the tax collector and with him<sup>as</sup> was the carriage (Taboot), the tax collector said to Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, ‘Open this carriage (Taboot) until whatever is in it gets displayed’. So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said to him: ‘Say whatever you like with regards to it, from the gold or the silver and I<sup>as</sup> shall pay it as tax, but do not open it’. The tax collector refused until he opened it, and Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> was angry over its opening.

So when Sara came out, and she had good qualities and was very beautiful, the tax collector said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘What is (the relationship of) this woman to you<sup>as</sup>?’ Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said; ‘She is my<sup>as</sup> sanctity (Hurmat i.e. wife) and the daughter of my<sup>as</sup> aunt’. 
So the tax collector said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘So what made you<sup>as</sup> to place her in this carriage (Taboot)?’ Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said: ‘The honour (Ghairat) against anyone looking at her’. So the tax collector said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘I will not leave you<sup>as</sup> to depart until I let the king know of her condition and yours<sup>as</sup>’.

So he sent a messenger to the king, who let him know, and the king sent a messenger from him telling them to bring him<sup>as</sup> to him. So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said to them: ‘I<sup>as</sup> will not separate from the carriage (Taboot) even if my<sup>as</sup> soul separates from my<sup>as</sup> body’. So they informed the king about that, and the king sent a message that they should bring him<sup>as</sup> and the box with him<sup>as</sup>.

So they took Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, and the carriage (Taboot), and all what was with him<sup>as</sup> until they came up to the king. The king said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘Open the carriage (Taboot)!’ So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O king! In it is my<sup>as</sup> sanctity (Hurmat i.e. wife), the daughter of my<sup>as</sup> aunt, and I<sup>as</sup> am prepared to ransom all what is with me<sup>as</sup>’.

The king got angry and forced Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> to open it. So when he saw Sara, he could not control his foolishness, and extended his hand towards her. Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> turned his<sup>as</sup> face away from her and from him due to his<sup>as</sup> honour (Ghairat) from it, and said: ‘Our Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Withhold his hand from my<sup>as</sup> sanctity (Hurmat i.e. wife) and daughter of my<sup>as</sup> aunt!’ So his hand could not arrive to her nor would it return back to him.

So the king said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘Was it your<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Who did this to me?’ He<sup>as</sup> said to him: ‘Yes. Surely, my<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> is Honourable (Ghayyour). He<sup>azwj</sup> Abhors the Prohibited, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is the One Who Made this situation between you and what you intended from the Prohibited’.

The king said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘So supplicate to your<sup>as</sup> God that He<sup>azwj</sup> should Return my hand back to me. If He<sup>azwj</sup> Answers you<sup>as</sup>, I will never present (myself) to her’. Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said: ‘My<sup>as</sup> God! Return his hand back to him, so that he would refrain from my<sup>as</sup> sanctity (Hurmat i.e. wife)’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Returned his hand back to him.

The king came near to her and looked at her, then extended his hand around her. So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> turned his<sup>as</sup> face away from it due to his<sup>as</sup> honour (Ghairat) from it, and said; ‘Our Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Withhold his hand from her! So his hand withered and could not arrive to her.

So the king said to Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, ‘Surely your<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> is Honourable (Ghayyour) and so are you, so supplicate to your God that He<sup>azwj</sup> should return my hand back to me, for it is an action that I shall not repeat. Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said to him: ‘I<sup>as</sup> will ask Him<sup>azwj</sup> upon the condition that you will not ask me<sup>as</sup> again to supplicate to Him<sup>azwj</sup>’. The king said, ‘Yes’.
So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said: ‘Our Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If he is truthful, Return his hand! His hand returned back to him.

So when the king saw that from the honour which he had never seen before, and saw the Sign in (the return of) his hand, he magnified Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, and endowed him<sup>as</sup> (with gifts), and honoured him<sup>as</sup>, and let him<sup>as</sup> leave and said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘I grant you<sup>as</sup> safety from displaying her, or for anything else which is with you<sup>as</sup>. So go to wherever you like, but I have a need from you<sup>as</sup>’. Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said: ‘What is it?’

He said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘I would love it if you<sup>as</sup> would permit me that I should give her an attendant who is a Coptic woman who has beauty and intellect, who will serve her’. So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> gave him permission for that. So he called for her, and gifted her to Sara, and she is Hajar, mother of Ismail<sup>as</sup>.

Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> travelled with all of what was with him<sup>as</sup>, and the king came out with him, walking behind Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, in respect of Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> and for his<sup>as</sup> prestige. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Revealed to Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>: “Pause, and do not walk in front of the domineering tyrant and he walks behind you<sup>as</sup>, but make him to be in front of you<sup>as</sup> and walk, and show him respect, and prestige, for he is domineering, and it is necessary for there to be authorities in the earth, be they righteous or immoral”.

So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> paused and said to the king: ‘Wait, for my<sup>as</sup> God has revealed unto me<sup>as</sup> at this very moment that I<sup>as</sup> should show you respect, and honour you, and make you to walk in front of me<sup>as</sup>, and I<sup>as</sup> should walk behind you, due to your majesty’. So the king said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘This has been Revealed unto you<sup>as</sup>?’ Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said to him: ‘Yes’.

So the king said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘I testify that surely your<sup>as</sup> God is Friendly, Lenient, generous, and that you are making me incline towards your<sup>as</sup> Religion’. And the king bade farewell to them.

So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> journeyed until he<sup>as</sup> encamped at the high place of Syria, and left behind Lut<sup>as</sup> in the lower valleys of Syria. Then, when the birth of a son was delayed, Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said to Sara: ‘If you want, you can sell Hajar to me<sup>as</sup>, perhaps Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Grant us the sustenance of a son from it, who would become a successor for us’. So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> bought Hajar from Sara. He<sup>as</sup> went to her, and she gave birth to Ismail<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 561. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al-Husayn Bin Saeed, together from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Bin Ahmad Al-Munqary, from Yunus Bin Zabyaan who said:
‘I said to Abu Abdullah (a.s.), Why do you (a.s.) not forbid these two men from (criticising) this man?’
So he (a.s.) said: ‘Who is this man, and who are these two men?’
I said, ‘Why do you (a.s.) not forbid Hujr Bin Zaida, and Aamir Bin Juza’at, from (criticising) Al-Mufazzal Bin Umar?’
So he (a.s.) said: ‘O Yunus! I (a.s.) had asked these two to refrain from it, but they did not do it.
So I called the two of them over, and asked both of them, and wrote to both of them telling them what I (a.s.) needed from both of them, but they still did not restrain themselves from it.
So, may Allah (azwj) not Forgive them both, for by Allah (azwj), there are many honourable ones in his cordiality than these two regarding what they are impersonating from my (a.s.) cordiality.

Where he has said, ‘Why does she think by the absence that I do not love her?’, then the two of them have not honoured me (a.s.), but by Allah (azwj), had they both loved me (a.s.), they would have loved the one whom I (a.s.) love’.
